primitives.name: Baseball Ground Geometry
primitives.verbatim_quote: BASE-BALL—FOR THE PLAYER THE GROUND AND THE OUTFIT HILE laying out a base-ball ground is quite a task, it is not more difficult than marking tennis-courts, and the result is much more lasting.
primitives.assumptions: Euclidean plane geometry, fixed rectangular grandstand/backstop, standard baseball rulebook constraints.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Non-Euclidean curvature effects become significant on planetary scales; local flatness assumption holds for typical ballparks.

layer2.mapping: GSI: Spatial layout priors for pitch tracking systems. GSE: Geometric state transitions for player positioning and defensive shifts.
layer2.telemetry: Pitch trajectory coordinates (x,y,z), player positions (x_i, y_i)

primitives.name: Home Plate Placement
primitives.verbatim_quote: The back-stop is usually the front of the "grand stand," or a convenient fence; and the rules provide that the back-stop must be at least ninety feet behind the home plate.
primitives.assumptions: Backstop is perfectly parallel to the line between first and third base; perpendicular offset is exactly 90 feet.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Atmospheric turbulence causes pitch drift beyond approximately 60 feet; batter reaction time limits effective resolution.

layer2.mapping: GSI: Camera calibration for home plate zone boundaries. GSE: Pitch arrival timing states relative to batter stance.
layer2.telemetry: Camera focal length, pixel coordinates of home plate edges

primitives.name: Second Base Location
primitives.verbatim_quote: By fastening a tape at the home plate, and carrying it out 127 feet 4 inches in a straight line into the field, the position of the second base is found.
primitives.assumptions: Standard diamond shape with right angles at home and first/third bases; Pythagorean theorem holds exactly.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Field surface irregularities cause small deviations from ideal square geometry.

layer2.mapping: GSI: Diamond geometry priors for infield coverage models. GSE: State transitions for base-running trajectories.
layer2.telemetry: Distance measurements from home plate to second base

primitives.name: First/Third Base Locator
primitives.verbatim_quote: Then, seizing the line in the middle, carry it out first at one side, and then on the other, and where it is taut the locations of the first and third bases are determined.
primitives.assumptions: String tension is uniform along its entire length; geometric construction yields exact intersection points.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Material elasticity causes slight variations in string length under different tensions.

layer2.mapping: GSI: Trilateration algorithms for player tracking. GSE: Geometric state classification for force plays.
layer2.telemetry: String midpoint coordinates, tension force measurements
